artboards.title: C · The break, for whoever called it
D · The break, for everyone else

annotations.text:
Stopping, and getting up.

Two things a table needs that the game did not have: a way to hold everything for a moment, and a way to leave without ending the evening for everyone else.

The break is a timer, not a vote. Any phone can call one — and because stopping the room stops it for everyone, the button asks first (B). Then the round clock freezes where it stands, every screen goes grey, and after half a minute the game starts itself again, so a break nobody ends cannot strand the table. Another press adds another half minute, up to five. Cutting it short belongs to whoever called it (and to the host), because a break is somebody's minute and not the table's to take back. Everyone else gets the generous button instead: +30.

Leaving lives inside the break, in red — one tap to stop the room, one to go, and the screen that says what it costs (E). That is deliberate: you cannot leave the table by mis-tapping, and the table has already stopped to notice.

What the rest see is F: one ink toast, and the round dealt again under the same number with the next giver. A group keeps playing with whoever is left; a seat that empties comes off the board. Down to one seat and the game is called there — that state reuses the existing end screen, so it is not drawn here.

Every value is lifted from public/style.css and the faces are the real ones out of public/art.js — the boards are generated by design/pause/build.js, so they cannot drift from the phone.
